objective: Determine exact sine and cosine values using coordinates, symmetry, reference angles, and quadrant signs.

sources.title: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e, 7.3 Unit Circle
sources.use: Scope and optional reading. Explanations, examples, questions and diagrams are original.

instructionOutline: Turn a right triangle into a coordinate definition
Read cosine first and sine second
Derive the thirty-degree and sixty-degree points
Use the axes as exact anchors
Choose signs from the terminal location
Find the reference angle before the magnitudes
Separate a negative rotation from a negative coordinate
Remove whole turns without changing the point
Reflect a point across the horizontal axis
Reflect across the vertical axis or through the origin
Distinguish a shared coordinate from a shared terminal point
Use the circle equation as an identity
Recover a coordinate and justify its sign
Keep both possibilities when a quadrant is missing
Normalize a point on a larger circle
Distinguish exact values from numerical checks

checkpointPolicy.pass: All four questions and all their parts must be correct without hints.
checkpointPolicy.sampling: Every form includes a non-axis exact pair with reference angle, a negative directed angle, an axis point, and a signed coordinate reconstruction. Other practice variants support these objectives but are not separately certified by a four-question form.
checkpointPolicy.assistedWork: Guided work, investigation and practice do not award independent evidence.

generatorRules: Grade rational numbers and radicals by exact equivalence. Never accept a nearby decimal in place of an irrational value.
Use exact angle reduction in degrees, radians and turns. Reject unsupported investigation angles with a clear scope message; do not round them to a special angle.
Reuse the existing standard-angle values and independently verify all sixteen positions, periodicity and the circle identity.
Make coordinate order explicit in every pair. Include non-diagonal angles so swapping coordinates fails.
Test every quadrant and all four axes. Axes belong to no quadrant and have no acute reference angle.
A negative input is a direction, not an instruction to negate both coordinates.
Reconstruction must check the given sign against the open quadrant, form 1 minus the given square, retain both square-root candidates and then choose the justified sign.
Include rational and radical givens, insufficient information, out-of-range data and contradictory quadrant data.
Shuffle choice options deterministically without changing their stable answer IDs.
Normalize non-unit coordinates before reading sine and cosine. Preserve the distinction between a coordinate, a side length and a dimensionless ratio.

sequence: Select one of six cases or type an exact supported angle in degrees, radians or turns.
Predict the location and both coordinate signs before displaying the terminal point.
Enter the exact ordered pair, then compare a labeled diagram, an accessible coordinate table, the reference angle and the identity.
Compare the same point after one turn with its reflection across the horizontal axis.
Explain which coordinate changes under reflection and why the identity alone does not select signs.
Clear all dependent feedback when the angle, units, case or a prediction changes.
investigation.accessibility: Labeled native controls; keyboard operation; non-color sign labels; exact text and table alternatives to the diagram; live feedback; focusable scroll region; mobile layout and sticky-header clearance.
investigation.limits: The exact-angle investigation covers multiples of 30 or 45 degrees and the axes, with the existing rotation magnitude limit. This is a tool limit, not a restriction on the domains of sine and cosine.

verificationPlan: Independent exact table and trigonometric numerical cross-checks across signed full turns and all units.
Independent rational and radical reconstruction cases, invalid boundaries, signs, non-real data and unsupported nested radicals.
All 32 practice variants across varied deterministic seeds, equivalent answers and deliberate sign/order/rounding mistakes.
Checkpoint composition, every critical failure, hint independence and immutable attempt snapshots.
Lesson schema, rendered mathematics, topic-example-practice coverage and correct guided work.
Browser journeys for guided errors, all six cases, typed equivalent units, invalid inputs, stale-state clearing, keyboard, desktop/mobile accessibility, notes, hints, reload and export/restore.
Lint, TypeScript, production build and relevant shared storage/catalog regressions before activation.
